messages:
emily_support: Heads-up — enterprise customer on Dedicated reported partial final token after automatic reconnect. They see the stream end early and then a reconnect yields the same last few tokens twice. Repro attached.

raj_devx: Can you paste SDK version + minimal repro? Also did they use httpx or requests? Any proxy/LB in path?

emily_support: SDK v0.9.12 (py). They use our python async iterator with httpx AsyncClient, sometimes canceling the task at ~1.2s. Repro below:
```
# repro.py
import asyncio
from redwood import StreamingClient

async def run():
  c = StreamingClient(api_key="REDACTED")
  async for chunk in c.stream(model="rwd-large", prompt="hi"):
    print(chunk)
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)

asyncio.run(run())
```
Behavior: when client cancels (CTRL-C or task.cancel()) mid-stream, server logs show flush not completed and connection closed. After reconnect, iterator either replays duplicate tail tokens or drops final punctuation. Pinning to 0.9.10 didn't reproduce.

dan_eng_runtime: Could be CancelledError handling at the transport layer resulting in a half-flushed buffer being marked "sent" incorrectly. We need the request_id and server traces for that session.

emily_support: Customer provided x-request-id=rid-9bf2 and a short server log snippet: "stream: buffer_flush timeout, conn_id=42, request=rid-9bf2, state=closing" and "conn closed by client: CANCELLED". They also observed an HTTP/2 RST_STREAM from their LB.

raj_devx: Thanks. Please try reproducing with raw httpx (bypassing SDK yield/iterator wrapper) and also try socket-level abort to isolate whether the SDK iterator logic is introducing duplication. Include exact headers (Authorization, x-request-id, user-agent).

emily_support: Quick test: using httpx AsyncClient + cancelling task reproduces partial output ~3/5 runs. Minimal snippet used in repro attached to the ticket.

sre_bot: Incident INC-2026-114 created for Dedicated us-west-2. Linked customer ticket TKT-7423 and captured logs.

dan_eng_runtime: Working hypothesis: resume path uses KV-cache + replay that assumes server completed final flush. If client cancels mid-flush, server marks stream closed and on resume replays the last N tokens or drops last tokens because flush was incomplete. Patch idea: treat client CANCELLED as soft-close and force a synchronous buffer flush with a short grace period before marking stream-terminal. I'll try to build a local harness that cancels at precise offsets.

lina_support: Assigned to dan_eng_runtime. Emily, pls gather the python stacktrace from the client side, enable DEBUG for redwood.sdk, and ask customer for tcpdump/pcap if allowed. That will help determine whether the RST came from LB or client.

emily_support: On it. ETA ~2 hours — I'll post repro artifacts (httpx script, logs, small recording).

dan_eng_runtime: If we confirm a server-side race, plan: (1) implement guard to finish buffer flush or drop-in a flush marker on CANCEL, (2) create E2E tests that inject CancelledError at various token offsets, (3) backport hotfix to 0.9.x (target 0.9.13), (4) docs note about safe client cancellation patterns. :eyes:

emily_support: Thanks — marking as high-priority for the customer (SLA).
